_about: Persecution-onset table. Configurable and extensible: institutions whose collections touch territories or dates not covered here should add entries rather than relying on this default. Every entry must carry a source. Dates are transcribed from the table in the project methodology notes; where that table gives a month or a month range rather than a day, onset_earliest/onset_latest express that imprecision instead of inventing a day.
_structure: Each territory carries one or more `windows`. A window runs from its onset to `ends` (defaulting to risk_band_end). `presumption_tier` is normally `by_nuremberg_threshold`, meaning the tier is derived from the transfer's position relative to heightened_presumption_from. A window may instead set an explicit `ordinary` or `heightened` tier where the territory's own chronology, not the Nuremberg threshold, governs — see Italy.
_review_status: NOT reviewed by an admitted lawyer or a professional provenance researcher. The territory list and onset dates are transcribed from the project methodology notes; the Italy two-window model is a modeling decision made during implementation and needs expert confirmation.

risk_band_end.rationale: The risk band is deliberately extended past 1945. Post-war Collecting Point restitutions, internal-restitution failures in France and the Netherlands, and the 1948-1954 dispersal of 'heirless property' form a distinct and heavily contested band that a 1945 cut-off misses entirely.
risk_band_end.source: Project methodology notes, Heuristic Layer; Terezin Declaration (2009) on heirless property.

heightened_presumption_from.label: Nuremberg Laws
heightened_presumption_from.rationale: Under REAO Art. 3 this is the threshold at which the presumption of a persecution-related loss becomes the heightened presumption (verschaerfte Vermutung), rebuttable only on proof of fair value, free disposal of the proceeds, and that the transfer would have occurred absent persecution.

match_note: match_terms are matched case- and accent-insensitively on word boundaries against the record's `location` field. They are name variants of the same territory (English/German/local forms), not additional territories. Adding a territory means adding an entry with its own cited onset date.

territories._note: Modelled as two windows because the Nuremberg threshold does not describe Italy's chronology. The 1938 racial laws (leggi razziali) began civil and property restriction; the September 1943 occupation is where persecution escalates to deportation-level. Applying the global 15 Sept 1935 threshold would report every 1938-1943 Italian transfer at the heightened tier, which overstates what the 1938 laws support; omitting the 1938 window entirely would under-flag that period, which is the more dangerous error. This split is an implementation-time modelling decision and needs confirmation by a provenance researcher or an admitted lawyer.

windows.tier_basis: the tier is set explicitly for this window: the 1938 racial laws established civil and property restriction, and the Nuremberg threshold does not govern the Italian chronology
